notes.japanese: 中にゐる雛や卵を、そのまゝ蒸殺してしまふかと思はれる
notes.problem: ‘like to’ reads as ‘enjoy’ rather than ‘likely to’, so the nest image misfires.
notes.span: like to steam the chicks and eggs inside them alive where they lay
notes.suggestion: seemed likely at this rate to steam the chicks and eggs inside alive where they lay
notes.sureness: Sure; any native reader will trip on ‘like to’ here.

notes.japanese: 朱柄の麈尾をふりふり、裸の男にたからうとする虻や蠅を追つてゐた
notes.problem: ‘flourishing’ sounds showy, not the patient shooing of flies.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; ‘flourish’ almost always implies display.

notes.japanese: 鼠の尻尾のやうな髯を、申訳だけに生やして
notes.problem: ‘by way of apology’ suggests he is apologising, when the point is a token, scanty beard, and the inversion reads backwards.
notes.span: by way of apology, a beard like a rat's tail
notes.suggestion: a mere token of a beard on the tip of his chin, like a rat's tail
notes.sureness: Sure about the misreading; wording could be settled by the faithful reader confirming ‘mōshiwake dake ni’ means token.

notes.japanese: 人並をはづれた酒量である
notes.problem: ‘measure’ is dictionary-flat for drinking capacity and stops the sentence.
notes.span: was a measure beyond ordinary men
notes.suggestion: was a capacity beyond ordinary men
notes.sureness: Sure; ‘measure’ for 酒量 is not idiomatic English here.

notes.japanese: 暑さうに肥つた体を起しながら
notes.problem: ‘that looked hot of itself’ is unidiomatic and has to be read twice.
notes.span: raising his fat body that looked hot of itself
notes.suggestion: heaving up his fat body, hot-looking in itself,
notes.sureness: Sure this is translationese; exact shade could be checked against the Japanese.

notes.japanese: 殆、奇蹟に近い噂が盛に行はれてゐる
notes.problem: ‘abroad in full force’ is tangled and archaic; the rumour sentence collapses under it.
notes.span: rumours all but miraculous were abroad in full force
notes.suggestion: rumours all but miraculous were going round in full force
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; the sense is clear but the phrasing is not prose a writer would sign.

notes.problem: ‘cut amethysts’ in the plural sounds like loose jewels, not eyes.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; would want a check that 紫石稜 means a cut or faceted stone.

notes.japanese: こつちから頭を下げて
notes.problem: ‘from his own side’ is literal Japanese and means nothing in English.
notes.span: bowed his head from his own side
notes.suggestion: Liu was the first to bow his head
notes.sureness: Sure; this is stiffness from literalness, not the author.

notes.japanese: 身動きをしてはいけないと云ふので
notes.problem: ‘saying he must not move’ leaves unclear who must not move.
notes.sureness: Sure; plain ambiguity for an English reader.

notes.japanese: 普通の人間が、学校の教育などをうけるのも
notes.problem: ‘receive a schooling and the like’ is stiff and unidiomatic.
notes.span: receive a schooling and the like
notes.suggestion: go through schooling and the like
notes.sureness: Sure; ‘receive a schooling’ is not natural English.

notes.japanese: 皮膚自身は、それに対して、毫も弾力を持つてゐない
notes.problem: ‘not a hair of spring’ is a word-for-word rendering of elasticity that stops a reader cold.
notes.span: while the skin itself had not a hair of spring to answer them
notes.suggestion: while the skin itself had not an ounce of elasticity to answer them
notes.sureness: Sure; the faithful note can confirm 弾力 is elasticity.

notes.japanese: 急に落ちつけてゐた尻を持ち上げて
notes.problem: ‘the haunches he had settled’ is unidiomatic body English.
notes.span: lifted the haunches he had settled
notes.suggestion: raised himself from his settled squat
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; sense is getting up from squatting, wording needs the desk.

notes.japanese: 肉の色が朱泥に似た、小さな山椒魚のやうなもの
notes.problem: Double ‘like’ — ‘like a small salamander, the colour … like red mud’ — clutters a key sighting.
notes.span: the colour of its flesh like red mud
notes.suggestion: its flesh the colour of red mud
notes.sureness: Sure on the English clutter; zoology to be confirmed by faithful reader.

notes.japanese: 一年の中に、何度、床につくか、わからない位ださうである
notes.problem: Passive and wordy; the flat report of decline has to be read twice.
notes.span: and there is said to be no counting how many times in the year he now takes to his bed
notes.suggestion: and they say there is no counting how many times in a year he now takes to his bed
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; simpler syntax keeps the flat report without adding pathos.

notes.japanese: 偶、暗愚の蛮僧に遇つた為に、好んで、この天与の福を失ふやうな事になつた
notes.problem: ‘By chancing … willingly’ contradicts itself in English and sounds archaic.
notes.span: By chancing to meet an ignorant barbarian monk, he willingly brought about the loss of this heaven-given fortune
notes.suggestion: Through meeting by chance with an ignorant barbarian monk, he willingly threw away this heaven-given fortune
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; the odd pairing is in the source, but ‘by chancing’ is not English.

data.say: The English carries the tableau and the body well but is tripped throughout by small literalisms and dictionary words that a copy-edit for idiom would clear.
